thread:
Sara (AM): Heads-up — enterprise POC with Orion Health. During the test today streaming responses dropped mid-document and the client gets partial JSON. Customer is behind a corporate proxy/F5. Demo is Friday EOD, they're blocked. Req id: req_9a83b. Logs pasted below.

Devon (SE): Thanks — is this via SSE/EventSource in the browser or our streaming SDK over websockets? Any repro steps?

Sara (AM): Browser EventSource via the hosted API. They see multiple message events but the final chunk is truncated so JSON.parse fails. Network tab shows 200 then stream closed at ~12s.

Ali (Infra): Can you grab the raw response body for req_9a83b? Also check if the proxy is doing any buffering or has idle timeouts < 30s. Corporate LB often closes idle connections.

Sara (AM): Attaching snippet from their dev tools: 

```
event: message
data: {"id":"msg_1","text":"partial...\n```

then nothing. Client error: "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input".

Marco (SRE): That looks like proxy buffering + chunk coalescing issue. Some LBs buffer until they see enough bytes and then drop connection if they think body complete. Workarounds: disable proxy buffering or send periodic SSE comment heartbeats (": keepalive\n\n"). Also confirm Transfer-Encoding: chunked is preserved.

Devon (SE): Quick repro we can ask customer to try: curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=small&stream=true" | sed -u 's/^/<< /' — see whether chunks arrive incrementally. If curl shows full payload but browser doesn't, it's definitely proxy/browser pipeline.

Katie (Solutions): Short-term options for demo: 1) Use non-streaming mode (stream: false) and fetch final response (slower but reliable). 2) Ask customer infra to set `proxy_buffering off` (nginx) or `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. 3) Add heartbeat comments from our side every 10s to keep connection alive.

Devon (SE): Also check for our per-connection rate limiter that can reset connections when many small chunks look like abusive patterns. I'll validate logs for `limiter.reset` for req_9a83b.

Ali (Infra): Nginx snippet we can share: 

```
location /proxy/ {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
}
```

For F5, customer might need to increase TCP idle timeout and disable HTTP chunk consolidation.

Sara (AM): Can you drop that nginx snippet into the thread? Customer ops will try it. Also they asked if we can push a temporary change server-side to emit heartbeats.

Marco (SRE): We can add a short-term toggle on the gateway to emit `:hb\n\n` every 8s for streams flagged `demo_keepalive=true`. Low-risk and reversible. I'll schedule a small deploy if you confirm.

Devon (SE): If we do that, also include a minimal chunk-id header per message to help customers reassemble: `X-RW-Chunk-Id: <seq>` and expose `x-rw-debug` query param that turns on per-chunk ids in body. That will help debugging.

Sara (AM): Customer agreed to try nginx change now. They're also asking about pricing impact if we switch them to Dedicated for the demo to avoid network weirdness.

Katie (Solutions): For short demo, Dedicated is probably overkill. Offer mitigate steps first (nginx change + server heartbeat). If they want dedicated later we can present pricing options.

Devon (SE): Steps assigned: I will grep the logs for req_9a83b and paste server chunk stream. Marco — if you can enable the temporary keepalive toggle that would be ideal. Ali — can you prepare the nginx + F5 guidance doc.

alerts-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-123 streaming-demo-blocker — assigned to Marco.

Marco (SRE): I'll push a small toggle to staging and post rollout instructions. ETA 90m. If staging looks good I'll promote to canary and tag the customer-specific stream.

Sara (AM): Thanks all — scheduling a screenshare with Orion ops at 15:00 today to apply nginx change and test. Leaving this thread open; will post results. :thumbsup:

Devon (SE): If the nginx change doesn't work, next call will be to try non-stream mode for demo and continue postmortem.

Sara (AM): Update 15:42 — customer applied `proxy_buffering off` and stream is now stable for multiple 45s responses. They also saw the heartbeat comments we put on canary and that prevented mid-doc closes. Demo Friday still on. Closing blocker unless new issues crop up.

Marco (SRE): Marking fix as workaround in internal KB and scheduling a follow-up to add production keepalive toggles and docs for customers behind managed LBs.

Katie (Solutions): I'll draft the customer-facing guidance and pricing note for Dedicated if they ask.

Sara (AM): Great work, team. :tada:
